Apple last week released a carrier settings update to address cellular network issues for some AT&T iPhone 18 Pro Max users, and is now rolling out another carrier bundle update for devices running the iOS 27.2 beta. Here are the details.

Apple pushes AT&T carrier bundle update for iOS 27.2 beta

Last Friday, Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that a small number of AT&T iPhone 18 Pro Max users were experiencing an issue that could cause their devices to lose cellular service and be unable to make calls.

Apple said that iOS 27.0.1, along with a new carrier settings update, was issued to prevent the issue from affecting more devices. However, phones that have already lost service will still require a hardware replacement.

Tonight, as spotted by Aaron Perris on X, Apple began rolling out another carrier bundle update for AT&T iPhone 18 Pro Max users, this time specifically targeting devices running the iOS 27.2 beta.

Reports of the issue first surfaced in late September, when some AT&T iPhone 18 Pro Max users found that their devices suddenly could not make calls, send texts or use cellular data, with only "SOS" showing in the status bar.

Worth noting, the issue only affected iPhone 18 Pro Max units in the US using Qualcomm modems. The iPhone 18 Pro, which uses Apple's own C2 modem, was not affected.

Apple's carrier settings update last week bumped AT&T users on iOS 27.0 to version 72.1. However, those running the iOS 27.2 beta remain on the older 72.0.2 carrier bundle.

Tonight's update is reported to bump the carrier bundle on those devices to 72.0.3, likely extending Apple's modifications for AT&T to iPhone 18 Pro Max users testing the iOS 27.2 beta.
